opening: Over a smartphone, a daughter begs for a life to be spared and a kidnapper shouts: bring one hundred million yen alone by noon tomorrow, or this hostage dies; no police. Hearing the demand, her father decides the ransom should not be paid. Why?
solution: The father, not the daughter, is the hostage. The wealthy daughter receives the call and pleads for her father's life. Hearing her ordered to deliver the ransom alone, he believes the kidnapper will kill both of them to silence witnesses once she arrives. He tells her not to pay or come, sacrificing his own safety to protect his only family.

rubric.criterion: Father is hostage beside kidnapper; wealthy daughter is free on the other end, begging for father's life.
Demand that she bring ransom alone makes father fear the kidnapper will kill both to eliminate witnesses.
He opposes payment/arrival to protect his daughter, his only family, even at risk to himself; this is his feared outcome, not a reported double murder.

translation_notes: Role-neutral threat retained in English rather than adding a gendered hostage pronoun. Japanese title pun omitted from solver. Source opening says 100 million yen but long solution says 1 billion; normalize to opening amount and do not grade exact amount.
